text: The LORD said to Moses:
Speak to the whole congregation of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy.
Each of you shall revere his mother and his father, and you shall keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols, and do not make cast gods for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
When you offer a fellowship sacrifice to the LORD, offer it so that it will be accepted for you.
It shall be eaten on the day you sacrifice it, or on the next day; whatever is left over until the third day must be burned in the fire.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is tainted; it will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear his guilt, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD; that person shall be cut off from his people.
When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
Do not strip your vineyard bare or pick up the fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
You shall not steal. You shall not deceive or lie to one another.
You shall not swear falsely by my name and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not exploit your neighbor or rob him. Do not keep the wages of a hired worker with you until morning.

versions.text: You shall not exploit your neighbor or rob him. Do not hold back the wages of a hired worker overnight until morning.
versions.explanation: "overnight until morning" is redundant in English and stumbles when read aloud. The Hebrew תָלִין ("shall not stay the night") is fully carried by "until morning"; "keep with you" also reflects אִתְּךָ, which is currently unrepresented.

text: You shall not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind, but you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.
You shall not pervert justice. Do not show partiality to the poor or favoritism to the great, but judge your neighbor fairly.
You shall not go about spreading slander among your people, and you shall not stand by when your neighbor's life is at stake. I am the LORD.
You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You must surely rebuke your fellow Israelite, so that you do not bear sin because of him.

versions.text: You shall not hate your brother in your heart. Rebuke your neighbor honestly, so that you do not share in his guilt.
versions.explanation: The word "honestly" is not in the Hebrew; the doubled verb (infinitive absolute + finite) expresses emphasis or obligation, best rendered "you must surely rebuke" rather than adding a manner adverb.

versions.text: You shall not hate your brother in your heart. You must surely rebuke your neighbor, so that you do not share in his guilt.
versions.explanation: Two small refinements: (1) the Hebrew here uses 'amit ('fellow, associate'), a different word from re'a ('neighbor') used in v. 18; rendering both as 'neighbor' obscures the distinction. (2) The clause literally reads 'and you shall not bear sin on account of him' — the guilt incurred is the hearer's own, incurred by failing to reprove, rather than a sharing in the other person's guilt. Both current renderings are within the range of accepted interpretation, so this is an improvement rather than a correction.

text: You shall not take revenge or bear a grudge against the children of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
You shall keep my statutes. Do not mate different kinds of animals. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not wear a garment woven of two kinds of material.

If a man sleeps with a woman who is a slave promised to another man but who has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there must be an inquiry. They shall not be put to death, because she had not been freed.
The man shall bring his guilt offering to the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting: a ram as a guilt offering.
With the ram of the guilt offering the priest shall make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin he has committed, and the sin he committed will be forgiven him.
When you enter the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, regard its fruit as forbidden. For three years you are to consider it forbidden; it must not be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit shall be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that your harvest may increase. I am the LORD your God.
You shall not eat anything with the blood still in it. You shall not practice divination or seek omens.
You shall not cut the hair at the sides of your head or clip off the edges of your beard.
You shall not make gashes in your flesh for the dead or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not degrade your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and be filled with depravity.
You shall keep my Sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or spiritists; do not seek them out and be defiled by them. I am the LORD your God.
Stand up in the presence of the aged, show respect for the elderly, and fear your God. I am the LORD.
When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not mistreat him.
The foreigner living among you must be treated as one of your native-born. Love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
You shall not act dishonestly in judgment, in measures of length, weight, or volume.
Use honest scales and honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my statutes and all my ordinances, and do them. I am the LORD.
